anomalies.observed: On the CAN BUS schematic pages, both MCP2515 CAN controllers are wired with CAN_CIPO on pin 14 and CAN_COPI on pin 15 (U8: CAN_CIPO -> pin 14, CAN_COPI -> pin 15; U9: CAN_CIPO -> pin 14, CAN_COPI -> pin 15).
anomalies.expected: For an MCP2515, pin 14 is SI (SPI input from the host) and pin 15 is SO (SPI output to the host). Using the design's own SPI naming convention, CAN_COPI (Controller Out, Peripheral In) should connect to pin 14/SI and CAN_CIPO (Controller In, Peripheral Out) should connect to pin 15/SO.

evidence.quote: CAN BUS page: U8 (MCP2515-xSO) left-side labels show CAN_CIPO at pin 14 and CAN_COPI at pin 15; U9 (MCP2515-xSO) similarly shows CAN_CIPO at pin 14 and CAN_COPI at pin 15.
two isolated CAN buses (CAN0, CAN1), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller (U8, U9)
COPI "Controller Out, Peripheral In" CIPO "Controller In, Peripheral Out"

anomalies.impact: The SPI MOSI/MISO lines are swapped on both CAN controllers, so the CM4 cannot communicate correctly with U8 or U9. CAN0 and CAN1 would be nonfunctional, breaking the motor/actuator CAN interfaces and any e-stop signaling routed through those CAN connectors.

parsed.summary: An anomaly is detected: both MCP2515 CAN controllers have their SPI data lines reversed, with CAN_CIPO connected to SI pin 14 and CAN_COPI connected to SO pin 15, which prevents correct SPI communication with the CAN controllers.
